title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy setting for numeric-only meeting passcodes
summary: Hold: the admin-centre route omits the documented Edit step needed to open the selected policy. The open questions also leave delegated scheduling and admin-change auditing unresolved despite Microsoft documenting both at the meeting-policy and Teams-admin level. The passcode format, default, PowerShell control and roadmap details are supported.

claims.claim: Teams has a meeting-policy setting named Allow numeric-only meeting passcodes.
claims.quote: Allow numeric-only meeting passcodes | Off | Controls whether meetings use 8-digit numeric-only passcodes.

claims.claim: Enabling the setting makes affected meetings use 8-digit numeric-only passcodes.
claims.quote: Controls whether meetings use 8-digit numeric-only passcodes.

claims.claim: The system default is an 8-character alphanumeric meeting passcode.
claims.quote: Default: Alphanumeric passcodes with 8 characters (system default).

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The numeric-only control is off by default and requires administrator enablement, so admin-opt-in describes its arrival.
claims.quote: Changes apply only to meetings scheduled after the setting is enabled. Existing meetings are not affected. This setting is disabled by default.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The setting is on a meeting policy and affects meetings scheduled by users to whom that policy applies.
claims.quote: When enabled, meetings scheduled by users to whom this policy applies will use 8-digit numeric-only passcodes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The PowerShell reference says numeric-only passcodes do not align with Microsoft's recommended meeting security best practices.
claims.quote: Numeric-only passcodes increase the risk of unauthorized access compared to the default setting and do not align with Microsoft’s recommended meeting security best practices.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes tenant admins enabling the setting for meetings organised by selected users or groups.

claims.claim: The roadmap says enabling numeric-only passcodes displays a warning.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls: API and automation
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -PasscodeComplexity NumericOnly to enable numeric-only passcodes on an existing meeting policy.
claims.quote:
[-PasscodeComplexity <String>]
Specify the name of the policy being created.
NumericOnly: 8-digit numeric-only passcodes with lower complexity for meetings scheduled by users to whom this policy applies.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Setting -PasscodeComplexity Default restores the system-default alphanumeric format for newly scheduled meetings.
claims.quote:
Controls whether meeting passcodes use the system-default complexity or a reduced complexity using numeric-only digits.
Default: Alphanumeric passcodes with 8 characters (system default).

claims.claim: Users get the global meeting policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: A separate custom meeting policy can be assigned to chosen users to give them settings different from the global policy.
claims.quote: You can edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies. Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to the numeric-only passcode setting is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the licensing notes and licensing sentence with 'Users need a Microsoft Teams product license to use Teams, except when joining meetings anonymously. Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to the numeric-only passcode setting at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. In the cost rationale, replace 'a licence for this setting is not yet published' with 'no licence requirement specific to this setting is published'. Narrow the licensing open question to 'Will Microsoft publish a licence requirement specific to this setting?'

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no meter specific to this setting at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams numeric-only meeting passcodes licensing price meter Teams license meeting policy; numeric-only meeting passcodes license meter price limit. Read settings-policies-reference, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, user-access and Microsoft Teams add-on licenses.

claims.claim: The cited pages give no price for the numeric-only meeting passcode setting.
claims.quote: Searched: numeric-only meeting passcodes license meter price limit. Read settings-policies-reference, meeting-policies-overview, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and overview-meetings-events; none gives a price for this setting.

claims.claim: The cited pages give no credit rate for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams numeric-only meeting passcodes licensing price meter Teams license meeting policy. Read settings-policies-reference, meeting-policies-overview, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and overview-meetings-events; none gives a credit rate for this setting.

claims.claim: The cited pages give no usage or spending limit for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: numeric-only meeting passcodes license meter price limit. Read settings-policies-reference and the PasscodeComplexity section of Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, plus meeting-policies-overview and overview-meetings-events; no setting-specific usage or spending limit appears.

claims.claim: The cited meeting-policy pages do not specify the role needed to edit meeting policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams meeting policies role edit manage meeting policies administrator license. Read meeting-policies-overview and the cited setting and cmdlet sections: no named role there. using-admin-roles separately documents Teams admin roles; the claim is limited to the cited pages.

claims.claim: The briefing leaves the application of the meeting policy when an authorised delegate schedules on an organiser's behalf undocumented.
claims.quote: When a delegate authorized to send meeting invitations for someone else sends a meeting, the meeting policy applies to the person who granted the delegate permission.
claims.fix: Replace the delegated-scheduling open question with 'When an authorised delegate sends a meeting invitation for someone else, the meeting policy applies to the person who granted the delegate permission.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-who-can-schedule-meetings. Do not claim that the page separately documents a numeric-passcode-specific delegation exception.

claims.claim: Whether any audit event records an administrator changing this setting is presented as unpublished.
claims.quote: Teams Admin Action | TeamsAdminAction | Logged when a Teams admin performs actions like updating, adding, or deleting Teams related settings or configurations using admin tools like PowerShell, Admin Center, API, etc.
claims.fix: Replace the audit open question with 'Microsoft documents TeamsAdminAction for Teams administrators updating, adding or deleting Teams settings or configurations through PowerShell, the admin centre or APIs.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities#teams-activities. If retaining an open question, narrow it to 'Which event details identify a change to PasscodeComplexity?'
